card.text: M62 is a globular star cluster in the Milky Way, about 6,030 parsecs away.

sources.label: Baumgardt & Vasiliev (2021), Accurate distances to Galactic globular clusters through a combination of Gaia EDR3, HST and literature data, MNRAS 505, 5957; Baumgardt's orbits table, NGC_6266: Rsun 6.03 ± 0.09 kpc
Wikipedia, "Messier 62"
sources.quote: Messier 62 or M62, also known as NGC 6266 or the Flickering Globular Cluster, is a globular cluster of stars located in the south of the constellation of Ophiuchus.

introduction.text: M62 is drawn as 1,218 of its member stars, measured by Gaia; each dot sits at its sky position, at the cluster's distance.

sources.quote: The cluster was discovered on 7 June 1771 by Charles Messier, who listed it as the 62nd entry in his catalogue published eight years later.
